chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Abu al-Jawza, from al-Husayn ibn Ulwan, from Amr ibn Khalid, from Zayd ibn Ali, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Remove from the martyr the fur coat, the shoes, the beret, the turban, the belt, and the trousers, unless blood has touched them. If blood has touched them, they are left; and nothing tight is left upon him except that it is loosened.'

key_terms.الْفَرْوُ: A fur coat or garment with the wool still attached
key_terms.مَعْقُودٌ: Tied or knotted (referring to tight bindings)

ai.seo_question: What garments are removed or kept on a martyr during ritual burial preparation?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi, transmitted through the lineage of Imam Ali (AS), establishes the specific juristic protocol for preparing a martyr for burial, emphasizing the preservation of dignity by retaining blood-stained garments. It highlights the Shia scholarly distinction between the general rule of removing outer layers and the exception for items directly involved in the martyrdom, reflecting the physical reality of battle casualties. The instruction to loosen all bindings underscores the completeness of the ritual purification (ghusl) process for the deceased warrior.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from his father, from Abu Al Jawza, from Al Husayn Bin Ulwan, from Amro Bin Khalid, from Zayd Bin Ali, 
from his forefathers<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al Momineen<sup>asws</sup> aid: ‘

Remove from the martyr, the fur (coat), and the shoes, and the beret, and the turban, and the belt, and the trouser, unless if this has been hit by the blood. So if the blood has hit it, it would be left, and there would not be left upon him anything tight, except that it would be loosened’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from his father from abu al-Jawza’ from al-Husayn ibn ‘Ulwan from ‘Amr ibn Khalid from Zayd ibn Ali from his ancestors, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, who has said the following: “

’Amir al-Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘Skull-cap, shoes, turban, loincloth and trousers are removed from a martyr unless they have become bloody in which case, they are left with, him and everything tied down with him is turned loose and open.’”
